args.title: checkout-api unhealthy on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Response: rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent version that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (only us-east rolled back due to an orchestrator error) and was retried successfully. Post-rollback, checkout-api is healthy across all regions on v2.3.0 with an error rate of 0.2%. Follow-up needed: root-cause the v2.3.1 failure and the orchestrator rollout error before reattempting the release.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

1. **Diagnosed**: checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. The most recent release healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.

2. **Rolled back**: The first rollback attempt partially failed (us-east rolled back, then the orchestrator halted). I verified the mixed state and retried, completing the rollback to v2.3.0 in all regions.

3. **Verified**: checkout-api is now healthy in all regions on v2.3.0 with a 0.2% error rate.

4. **Opened incident**: INC-0001 (SEV2) is open for checkout-api, documenting the failure, the rollback (including the orchestrator error), and follow-up items — root-causing the v2.3.1 failure before any reattempt. (Note: the incident creation call returned a timeout, but I confirmed the incident was successfully created, so on-call has been paged only once.)
